note_on_method: Each venue page rests on two City of Rockville pages: the Pickleball Courts and Programs page, whose table under "Outdoor Pickleball Courts" counts the courts and answers the lighting question row by row, and the park's own place page, which gives the address under an "Address" heading and describes the park. The US Census address geocoder supplies the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, on price, on surface, on nets at three venues, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Four dedicated pickleball courts, lit, in a 7.5-acre sports park on Twinbrook Parkway.

The count is the City's own cell in its outdoor-courts table: "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", Lighted "Yes". Most of Rockville's pickleball is lines painted on tennis courts, and Broome is one of two venues where every court was built for the game. The park page counts "four pickleball courts" beside "two tennis courts", and its accessible-features table repeats it: "Four accessible pickleball courts."

The City calls the park "a 7.5-acre sports paradise next to the site of the former Edwin W. Broome Junior High School", with two lighted premier baseball fields "primarily used for league play", a futsal court and a playground.
slots.getting_there:
751 Twinbrook Parkway, Rockville, MD 20851, under the "Address" heading on the park's page. The US Census geocoder matched it at house-number level, as the City writes it, in Montgomery County inside the incorporated place Rockville city.

Parking is stated: "plenty of parking", with "Six accessible parking spaces." counted, and there are drinking fountains. Restrooms are not listed among the park's features.
slots.what_to_expect:
The City's rule is "Courts are open from dawn to dusk and are available on a first-come, first-served basis", and for this lit row it adds "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m.", so an evening game here is published rather than guessed. Four courts is enough for a rotation.

Two things cut the other way. "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts, so some may be reserved for class use and closed to the public", and the row's "View Schedule" link has not been read for this page. The row also says nothing about nets, so no net answer is published. No price is stated and no surface is named.

faqs.a: Four, all dedicated in the City's words: "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts". The park page counts them the same way.
Yes. The Lighted column reads Yes for this row, and the City adds that "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m."

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Not stated. The row says only "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", without the bring-your-own-net note the City attaches to its striped courts.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts painted on one tennis court in a 5.9-acre neighbourhood park in Twinbrook, unlit by the City's own answer, and reached on foot because the park has no parking.

The City's row reads "2 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; bring your own net)", Lighted "No". That is one tennis court carrying two pickleball games, each with a net the players bring. The park page says the same from the tennis end: "two tennis courts (one with pickleball lines)". Two courts is a game rather than a rotation, and with no lights it is a daylight game.

The rest of the park is a baseball field, a basketball court, a pavilion, a playground and wooded trails "linking Gladstone Drive and Baltimore Road". The City notes that "restrooms are available only with a permit".
slots.getting_there:
1248 Gladstone Drive, Rockville, MD 20851, under the "Address" heading on the park's page, matched at house-number level by the US Census geocoder in Montgomery County inside the incorporated place Rockville city.

The parking answer is a stated no: "Calvin Park does not have parking. Access to park amenities is available via pathways connecting to city sidewalks and roads." The City adds that "The park can also be accessed via the bike path along Baltimore Road." So plan to walk or ride in.
slots.what_to_expect:
A single tennis court doing duty as two pickleball courts, with whatever net you carried in. The City's rule applies: "Courts are open from dawn to dusk and are available on a first-come, first-served basis." There is no 10 p.m. extension: the Lighted column reads No, a stated negative rather than a gap.

Because the two courts share one tennis court, a tennis player who arrives first takes both. "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts", and the row's "View Schedule" link has not been read for this page. No price is stated and no surface is named.

faqs.a: Two, both painted on one tennis court: "2 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; bring your own net)". The park's second tennis court has no lines.
No. The City writes "Calvin Park does not have parking" and points to pathways from city sidewalks and roads, and to the bike path along Baltimore Road.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Yes. The City's row says "bring your own net", and the park page does not mention a net at all.

slots.description:
Five pickleball courts painted on three lit tennis courts in a 44.22-acre athletic park and forest preserve.

The five is the sum of two lines in one row of the City's table: "1 Pickleball Court (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; use tennis net)" and "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted "Yes". One tennis court is lined for a single game played over the tennis net; two more are lined for two games each with nets the players bring.

The park page calls them "three lighted tennis courts". Around them are ballfields, three lighted basketball courts, batting cages, two playgrounds and nature trails to Cabin John Creek.
slots.getting_there:
800 Monroe St., Rockville, MD, under the "Address" heading on the park's page, where the City prints the postcode 20852. The US Census geocoder matched the house number and street as written and answered 20850, which is the postcode published here, with the disagreement stated.

Parking is stated: "Dogwood Park offers plenty of parking", with "Six accessible parking spaces." counted. Restrooms are "available only with a permit" for the pavilion.
slots.what_to_expect:
Lit courts and a late finish. The rule is dawn to dusk, first come, first served, and for lit rows "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m."

The net arrangement is the thing to understand before you arrive. One tennis court is set up for one game over the tennis net, which needs nothing from you. The other two carry two games each and the City says "bring your own net" for those four. Turn up without a net and you are competing for one court out of five. These are tennis courts first. "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts". No price is stated and no surface is named.

faqs.a: Five, all on tennis courts: the City's row prints "1 Pickleball Court (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; use tennis net)" and "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)".

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: For one court, no: it is played over the tennis net. For the other four, yes. No single net answer is published for the venue.

faqs.q: Why does the postcode differ from the City's page?
faqs.a: The City prints 20852 with its address. The Census address file matched 800 Monroe St. as written and returned 20850, which is published here, with the disagreement noted.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts painted on two tennis courts in a 30.66-acre park beside Thomas Farm Community Center, unlit by the City's own answer.

The row reads "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted "No". Two games per tennis court, nets the players bring, and a lighting answer that is a stated no rather than a silence. The park page says "two tennis courts with pickleball lines" and counts "Two accessible tennis courts."

The City describes "a 30.66-acre park adjoining Thomas Farm Community Center" with a playground, outdoor fitness equipment, a pavilion, trails and a multipurpose field, and says it "connects with the 11-mile Millennium Trail".

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts painted on one tennis court in a 4.4-acre park on the western side of Twinbrook, unlit by the City's own answer.

The row reads "2 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; bring your own net)", Lighted "No". One tennis court, two pickleball games on it, nets the players bring. It is the only tennis court in the park, so there is no second slab to move to, and two courts is a game rather than a rotation.

The rest of the park is a basketball court, a baseball/softball field, a playground, a pavilion with picnic tables and a grill, and paved paths with benches. The pavilion can be rented, and "restrooms are available only with a permit".

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, two built for the game and two painted on a tennis court, in a 6.7-acre park in the Lincoln Park neighbourhood, unlit by the City's own answer.

The City spells the park Isreal, and this site follows it. Its row prints two lines: "2 Dedicated Pickleball Courts" and "2 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; bring your own net)", Lighted "No". The striped pair exists only in the table, on the one tennis court the park has.

The City describes "a newly constructed rentable pavilion with ADA-accessibility including picnic tables, grills, restrooms and landscaping", a playground installed in 2024 and a basketball court. The park adjoins the Lincoln Park Community Center.

357 Frederick Avenue, Rockville, MD 20850, under the "Address" heading on the park's page, matched at house-number level by the US Census geocoder in Montgomery County inside the incorporated place Rockville city, in the postcode the City prints.

slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts that are always pickleball courts, and two more that depend on the tennis court being free. The rule is "Courts are open from dawn to dusk and are available on a first-come, first-served basis", and the Lighted column reads No, so this is daylight play with a stated end.

The dedicated pair carries no net note; the striped pair says "bring your own net". slots.description:
Four dedicated pickleball courts, lit, in a 26.29-acre park at the north end of King Farm, and the venue where the City holds its social play four mornings a week.

The row reads "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", Lighted "Yes". The park page says "four lighted pickleball courts" and the accessible-features table "Four accessible pickleball courts." With Broome Athletic Park this is one of two Rockville venues where every court was built for pickleball.

The park opened in 2008 and is named for Mattie J.T. Stepanek, "a poet and peace advocate". It holds a Peace Garden with a bronze statue of Mattie and his service dog Micah, three outdoor stone chess boards, three lighted tennis courts, two lighted basketball courts and a fenced dog park.
slots.getting_there:
1800 Piccard Drive, Rockville, MD 20850, under the "Address" heading on the park's page; the banner prints only "Rockville, MD", so the Address block is the line to use. The US Census geocoder matched it at house-number level, as written, in the postcode the City prints.

Parking is stated: "Plenty of parking is available for easy access.", with "Eight accessible parking spaces." counted. Restrooms are not in the feature list.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts that are pickleball courts whenever you arrive, lit until 10 p.m. The City's rule is dawn to dusk, first come, first served, with "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m."

The social play sessions are the one busy time the City writes down anywhere in Rockville: social play, 10 a.m. to noon on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, with players rotated so everyone gets on court. If you want a game without bringing three friends, those are the mornings to come; if you want the four courts to yourselves, they are the mornings to skip.

Beyond that, "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts". The row says nothing about nets, so no net answer is published. No price is stated and no surface is named.

The City describes a park that "connects various streets and areas in the Twinbrook Neighborhood", containing the Rockcrest Ballet Center, "a new for 2024 playground", basketball courts and "paved paths connecting Broadwood Avenue to Ardennes Avenue".
